facts.statement: ACS project contract assigns execution coordination to ACS, continuity to PCM, issue recording to OIO, and writing/visual direction to CGM.
facts.boundary: Component ownership is not equivalent to validated adopter outcome.

facts.statement: Current public hotload spec describes full PCM, CGM, OIO and ACS runtime with PARTIAL on incomplete required installation.
facts.boundary: Requires actual source check and safe run on a target before claiming a supported installation outcome.

facts.statement: Owner considers the current ACS site substantially better than early versions but not final; preserve it as Baseline A.
facts.boundary: Owner qualitative assessment, not independent UX evidence or completed baseline capture.

facts.statement: Owner wants the reusable framing router built and stabilized before initiating another site-generation experiment.
facts.boundary: Working direction in current conversation, not approval to generate/deploy Version B.

facts.statement: Owner has identified the next output as an ACS market-facing Version B website, separate from current Baseline A.
facts.boundary: Authorizes framing work, not implicit story approval, ABA code generation or deployment.

facts.statement: Owner explicitly selected the individual builder experiencing repeated AI-agent handoff and reorientation work as the first intended audience for market-facing ACS Version B.
facts.boundary: This is accepted intended audience direction, not independent customer research, market demand evidence, positioning signoff or generation authorization.

facts.statement: Owner selected 'Return attention to actual project work' as the market-facing B lead benefit direction, while expressly requesting clarification rather than choosing a primary website CTA.
facts.boundary: Accepts only a qualitative direction. Does not substantiate time savings, choose exact headline/position, authorize CTA behavior, approve storyboard or permit ABA generation.

facts.statement: Owner clarified that the primary purpose of market-facing ACS Version B is to introduce the product quickly and relatably, then explain the human problem, market fit, solution, proof/sales opportunity, and technical detail.
facts.boundary: This approves the product-introduction objective and desired content concerns only. Suggested exact section order, headline, CTA, visuals and market claims are not thereby accepted.

decisions.statement: Market the integrated working surface, respecting the narrower ownership boundaries of each module.
Keep current live ACS website as untouched Baseline A until a recorded capture and owner-reviewed Version B brief exist.
decisions.reason: Make comparison fair and avoid repeating expensive rework.

decisions.statement: Lead Version B with the individual long-project builder burdened by agent handoffs, ownership and reorientation; keep engineering team lead as a secondary candidate.
decisions.reason: Explicit owner selection of individual builder and repeated handoff burden, recorded in issue #1. Lead-audience decision only.

decisions.statement: Proposed product-identifying hero for Version B visual study: 'A shared way of working for AI agents in your repository.' Explain integrated ACS pack and the approved attention-to-work benefit. Exact wording and position remain unapproved.
decisions.reason: Product-first visual candidate on ABA PR #64. Earlier 'Build with agents. Stop managing every handoff' remains a rejected-as-primary-hero candidate because it delayed product identification; neither exact copy is owner accepted.

decisions.statement: Primary market-page CTA objective, label, click behavior and side effects are UNDECIDED; owner requested clarification rather than choosing the previously offered walkthrough or documentation link.
decisions.reason: Q3 was explicitly not answered. Previous examples are not an accepted decision; do not design a CTA control or assume a preview, docs navigation or installation.

decisions.statement: Lead the ACS B benefit framing with returning the individual builder's attention to their actual project work, rather than promising measured savings or reducing the installed pack to continuity alone.
decisions.reason: Explicit Q2 owner selection, limited to intended strategic benefit direction; exact product positioning, copy and site are pending separate creative signoff.

decisions.statement: Make ACS Version B first and foremost a clear product introduction for the selected individual builder, using short plain-language explanation and an emotionally relatable problem, with supporting solution, proof/evaluation and technical depth.
decisions.reason: Explicit owner statement of marketing-page purpose. Recommended precise information architecture remains a proposal for independent creative review.

rejections.why: Do not generate a Version B website before the framing workflow and the creative direction have been reviewed.

scenes.question: What is ACS, is it for me, and why might it matter?
scenes.belief_change: Identify ACS as an integrated repository-installed multi-agent working arrangement and relate it to the independent builder's coordination burden within the first screen.
scenes.visual_job: Immediately show a concise, recognizable product category and a real project-facing example, paired with human benefit; do not delay product identification until scene 3.
scenes.media_contract: Conceptual storyboard; no visual assets generated or reviewed.

scenes.question: What keeps repeating across work sessions?
scenes.belief_change: See repeated handoffs, ownership, approvals and explanation as one pattern, beyond a single tool feature.
scenes.visual_job: Same maker across a few session boundaries; concrete friction beats rather than invented customer testimony.
scenes.media_contract: Conceptual storyboard; no visual assets generated or reviewed.

scenes.question: How does this arrangement concretely work inside a repository?
scenes.belief_change: Deepen understanding of the already-introduced repo-installed product rather than reveal its category for the first time.
scenes.visual_job: Repo-centered install surface showing durable records and participating systems; conceptual until actual captures are approved.
scenes.media_contract: Conceptual storyboard; no visual assets generated or reviewed.

scenes.question: How do four distinct systems help one project?
scenes.belief_change: Connect coordination, continuity/governance, issue provenance and content guidance into one installer contract without blending ownership.
scenes.visual_job: Four linked functions with their own source-owned names, not a dashboard claiming ACS implemented everything.
scenes.media_contract: Conceptual storyboard; no visual assets generated or reviewed.

scenes.question: What would change if I considered installing it?
scenes.belief_change: Understand prerequisites, deliberate install/check, READY vs PARTIAL, and permission boundaries.
scenes.visual_job: Show the documented prerequisites and READY/PARTIAL distinction as explanatory information; no implied walkthrough interaction or simulated live install.
scenes.media_contract: Conceptual storyboard; no visual assets generated or reviewed.

scenes.question: What proof and honest limitations let me evaluate it?
scenes.belief_change: Separate inspectable source-backed product behavior from buyer benefit hypotheses, independent research and installation limitations.
scenes.visual_job: Attach short evidence to relevant product claims and make deeper technical and compatibility docs available without front-loading an audit.
scenes.media_contract: Conceptual storyboard; no visual assets generated or reviewed.

scenes.question: What should I do next after understanding the product? OWNER CLARIFICATION PENDING.
scenes.belief_change: The visitor should eventually understand the next action and its actual outcome; no CTA is specified until Q3 is answered.
scenes.visual_job: Hold an explicit CTA-design slot open; do not draw a button, preview, setup link or assumed click flow.
scenes.media_contract: Draft placeholder depending on unanswered CTA Q3/D5. No CTA illustration, UI element, copy, asset or code authorized.

claims.wording: The ACS coordination runtime specifies join-order agent roles, boss lease and FIFO failover, claim ownership, watchdog signals and accepted proposals leading to PRs.
claims.limitations: Verified as described in pinned product/pack documentation; this is not a claim of measured adopter outcomes or a fresh install demonstration.

claims.wording: The integrated hotload pack declares pinned PCM continuity and delivery governance, OIO issue recording, CGM content guidance, and ACS execution coordination as distinct participating components.
claims.limitations: Describes the product contract, not ownership of PCM/OIO/CGM by ACS or proof all installations are presently compatible.

claims.wording: The installer/check flow is designed to reject incomplete required setup rather than reporting it as a complete install; installed features require prerequisites and version compatibility.
claims.limitations: Contract-described fail-closed behavior, not a verified successful install against an arbitrary repository.

claims.wording: ACS is a repo-installed coordination/hotload arrangement, not a hosted service or an autonomous decision-maker.
claims.limitations: Do not imply that a website preview installs, writes or starts a production agent session.
